summary: The third rhythm — a 94-second silent, single-world 3D film about why TOI-4342’s residual 18.9082-day signal remains a planet candidate.
content:
Learner and question: A curious secondary-school learner who understands circles, ratios and repeating patterns. Central question: How does masking two known planets reveal evidence for a possible third—and why is repetition insufficient for confirmation?

Reverse prerequisite design: Open on a spatial constellation rooted at “A third planet?” Work backward through “Repeated dimming”, “Orbit + sightline” and “Rule out impostors”. Repeated dimming requires “Light + blocked area” and “Period + phase”; orbit and sightline require “Projection + inclination”. Impostor testing depends on those same leaves plus checking where the light originates. These are dependencies, not independent proofs. Retreat to familiar light and shadows, then teach forward along the illuminated connections.

Forward teaching sequence, 94 seconds:
• 0–10: Title, TOI-4342 / TIC 354944123, and staged prerequisite constellation. Reveal labels successively.
• 10–25: Approach the mesh stellar sphere. A planet blocks a fraction of its projected luminous disk. Define transit, radius ratio k, and fractional depth. Show the sole main formula: δ ≈ (Rp/Rstar)² ≈ 0.001142. Label “Uniform-disk illustration”; this is not measured photometry.
• 25–39: Move sideways around the same geometry. Define sightline, projection and inclination. Demonstrate that a transit depends on observer position; the planet remains physically present behind the star. A projected ellipse remains a circular orbit in space.
• 39–54: Pull back to the orbital system. Define period as one circuit and phase as position within that cycle. Show b, c and the dashed “candidate” orbit with correct relative radii and angular speeds. Explicitly label circular orbits, arbitrary phases and coplanarity illustrative; overview body sizes exaggerated.
• 54–70: Represent successive brightness samples as beads along a spatial time strand beside the system. Mark known b/c transit windows, then exclude those samples before searching the remainder. Do not subtract invented dips or interpolate across masked gaps. Label sample geometry schematic. Repeated amber markers establish the 18.9082-day hypothesis; independent TOI-host recovery supports recurrence.
• 70–85: Revisit the impostor branch. Eight separated evidence points represent observing sectors, not eight transits. Introduce nearby-source checks and model-dependent false-positive probability without a dashboard or certainty meter.
• 85–94: Return to the unresolved root. Display “A candidate. Confirmation still needed.” Then name ground photometry, high-resolution imaging and radial velocities as follow-up routes, with a quiet final hold.

Terms and goals: Learners should explain blocked-area dimming, period versus phase, observer-dependent transit geometry, masking versus subtraction, and candidate versus statistical validation. Define sector as an observing interval and FPP as false-positive probability under the tested models, never detection confidence.

Mathematical acceptance: Use b/c periods 5.5382498/10.688716 days and original radii 2.266/2.415 Earth radii. With Mstar ≈ 0.63 solar masses, Kepler-derived circular distances are approximately 0.05252, 0.08141 and 0.11907 AU; label these model-derived. Radius ratios must be 1:1.55013:2.26735; angular-speed ratios 1:0.51814:0.29290. Transit closeup must use k = 0.0337894 and impact parameter 0.746895. Keep fitted duration 2.45559 hours and radius 2.207 (+0.112/−0.108) Earth radii distinct from the rounded overview model. FPP = 0.1113498 exceeds 0.015; low neighboring-source probability does not validate the signal.

Visual acceptance and boundaries: One ThreeDScene; sculptural meshes, spatial curves, stable geometric colors, deliberate depth-revealing camera moves and readable holds. At most one main formula and two caption lines simultaneously. No flat slides, full-screen charts, decorative torus, gravity well, measured orbital normals, official “d” designation or 47.5-day orbit. Optional S¹/S² labels describe path/surface only; topology proves nothing about candidacy. Omit the directional belt unless it earns its time; if used, calculate its transit half-angle and label visual widening. Reuse modest meshes, approximately 16×32 stellar patches; use move_camera/set_camera_orientation. Deliver 1280×720, 30 fps through Cairo, with continuous-motion review before claiming visual success.
